articles.title: Gitea Patches 27 Security Flaws, Including Critical SSH Authentication Bypass and SSRF
articles.summary: Gitea has released security updates addressing 27 reported flaws across versions 28.0.0 and 28.1.0, including a critical SSH authentication bypass and server-side request forgery (SSRF) weaknesses.
articles.content:
Gitea has released security updates addressing 27 reported flaws across versions 28.0.0 and 28.1.0, including a critical SSH authentication bypass and server-side request forgery (SSRF) weaknesses.

The fixes cover account access, repository permissions, automated workflows, and connections to internal systems. Administrators should treat the update as an urgent priority for their development infrastructure.

Released on September 30, Gitea 28.0.0 lists 20 CVEs in its security notes. The reported total of 27 spans that release and the follow-up 28.1.0 update, rather than 28.0.0 alone. Gitea also dropped its historical “1.” version prefix, making this release 28.0.0 instead of 1.28.0.

The standout issue, CVE-2026-103059, carries a CVSS score of 9.1 and affects deployments using Gitea’s built-in SSH server. Its public-key lookup used an SQL LIKE comparison that ignores letter case on some databases, including the default SQLite database. This could cause a specially crafted RSA key to match another user’s registered key.

An attacker who constructs a suitable case variant of a victim’s public key and derives its matching private key could authenticate as that victim.

This is not a general bypass using any altered key; the attacker must meet those key requirements. Gitea now identifies presented keys through their fingerprints, removing the unsafe text comparison.

## Gitea Patches 27 Security Flaws

Several patched flaws allowed repository migrations and mirrors to bypass outbound connection rules. CVE-2026-70357 involved a gap between hostname validation and the actual Git connection.

An attacker could change the hostname’s DNS response during that gap, directing Gitea toward an internal host after the initial security check passed.

CVE-2026-101027 allowed an approved domain to skip destination IP checks, while CVE-2026-101029 used multiple DNS answers to bypass the outbound allowlist.

Another flaw, CVE-2026-89430, let push mirrors connect to internal Git hosts after their saved addresses had passed an earlier check, potentially allowing forced pushes.

Gitea now routes Git network operations through an internal proxy that applies outbound access rules when connections occur. Administrators must review configuration changes before upgrading. For a deny-by-default policy, the release notes direct users to set EGRESS_MODE = strict and explicitly list allowed hosts.

The update also closes Gitea Actions approval gaps. CVE-2026-104632 allowed a canceled, approval-pending fork workflow to reach self-hosted runners when rerun.

CVE-2026-94205 checked only the event actor, allowing a maintainer-triggered event to run an untrusted contributor’s workflow without the required approval. Both checks are now tightened.

Other fixes address stored cross-site scripting in container blobs, duplicate Git tree entries that could hide malicious files from reviewers, and an installer flaw that issued an existing administrator’s session without checking the password. Permission fixes also remove lingering repository-transfer access and prevent deploy keys from inheriting repository-owner privileges.

Administrators should back up data, review breaking changes, and upgrade to 28.1.0. Gitea’s release notes explain the new network rules, Git 2.25 minimum, and changed workflow behavior.

ar.title: تقوم Gitea بتصحيح 27 عيبًا أمنيًا، بما في ذلك تجاوز مصادقة SSH الحرجة وSSRF
ar.summary: أصدرت Gitea تحديثات أمنية تعالج 27 عيبًا تم الإبلاغ عنها عبر الإصدارات 28.0.0 و28.1.0، بما في ذلك تجاوز مصادقة SSH الحرجة ونقاط الضعف في تزوير الطلب من جانب الخادم (SSRF).
ar.content:
أصدرت Gitea تحديثات أمنية تعالج 27 عيبًا تم الإبلاغ عنها عبر الإصدارات 28.0.0 و28.1.0، بما في ذلك تجاوز مصادقة SSH الحرجة ونقاط الضعف في تزوير الطلب من جانب الخادم (SSRF).

تغطي الإصلاحات الوصول إلى الحساب، وأذونات المستودع، وسير العمل الآلي، والاتصالات بالأنظمة الداخلية. يجب على المسؤولين التعامل مع التحديث كأولوية عاجلة للبنية التحتية للتطوير الخاصة بهم.

تم إصدار Gitea 28.0.0 في 30 سبتمبر، وهو يدرج 20 من التهديدات الخطيرة في ملاحظاته الأمنية. تم الإبلاغ عن إجمالي 27 امتدادًا لهذا الإصدار وتحديث المتابعة 28.1.0، بدلاً من 28.0.0 وحده. كما أسقطت Gitea رقمها التاريخي "1". بادئة الإصدار، مما يجعل هذا الإصدار 28.0.0 بدلاً من 1.28.0.

تحمل المشكلة البارزة، CVE-2026-103059، درجة CVSS تبلغ 9.1 وتؤثر على عمليات النشر باستخدام خادم SSH المدمج في Gitea. استخدم البحث عن المفتاح العام مقارنة SQL LIKE التي تتجاهل حالة الأحرف في بعض قواعد البيانات، بما في ذلك قاعدة بيانات SQLite الافتراضية. قد يتسبب هذا في تطابق مفتاح RSA المصمم خصيصًا مع المفتاح المسجل لمستخدم آخر.

يمكن للمهاجم الذي ينشئ نسخة مناسبة من المفتاح العام للضحية ويستمد مفتاحه الخاص المطابق أن يصادق على أنه الضحية.

هذا ليس تجاوزًا عامًا باستخدام أي مفتاح تم تعديله؛ يجب على المهاجم تلبية تلك المتطلبات الأساسية. يتعرف Gitea الآن على المفاتيح المقدمة من خلال بصمات الأصابع، مما يؤدي إلى إزالة مقارنة النص غير الآمنة.

## يقوم Gitea بتصحيح 27 عيبًا أمنيًا

سمحت العديد من العيوب المصححة لعمليات ترحيل المستودعات والمرايا بتجاوز قواعد الاتصال الصادر. يتضمن CVE-2026-70357 فجوة بين التحقق من صحة اسم المضيف واتصال Git الفعلي.

يمكن للمهاجم تغيير استجابة DNS لاسم المضيف خلال هذه الفجوة، وتوجيه Gitea نحو مضيف داخلي بعد اجتياز الفحص الأمني ​​الأولي.

سمح CVE-2026-101027 للنطاق المعتمد بتخطي عمليات التحقق من عنوان IP للوجهة، بينما استخدم CVE-2026-101029 إجابات DNS متعددة لتجاوز القائمة المسموح بها للصادرة.

عيب آخر، CVE-2026-89430، يسمح لمرايا الدفع بالاتصال بمضيفي Git الداخليين بعد أن اجتازت عناوينهم المحفوظة فحصًا سابقًا، مما قد يسمح بالدفع القسري.

يقوم Gitea الآن بتوجيه عمليات شبكة Git من خلال وكيل داخلي يطبق قواعد الوصول للخارج عند حدوث اتصالات. يجب على المسؤولين مراجعة تغييرات التكوين قبل الترقية. بالنسبة لسياسة الرفض الافتراضي، توجه ملاحظات الإصدار المستخدمين إلى تعيين EGRESS_MODE = صارمة وإدراج المضيفين المسموح بهم بشكل صريح.

يعمل التحديث أيضًا على إغلاق فجوات الموافقة على Gitea Actions. يسمح CVE-2026-104632 بسير عمل شوكة مُلغى وفي انتظار الموافقة للوصول إلى العدائين المستضافين ذاتيًا عند إعادة التشغيل.

قام CVE-2026-94205 بالتحقق من ممثل الحدث فقط، مما يسمح للحدث الذي يتم تشغيله بواسطة المشرف بتشغيل سير عمل مساهم غير موثوق به دون الموافقة المطلوبة. تم الآن تشديد كلا الشيكين.

تعالج الإصلاحات الأخرى البرمجة النصية المخزنة عبر المواقع في blobs الحاوية، وإدخالات شجرة Git المكررة التي يمكن أن تخفي الملفات الضارة عن المراجعين، وخلل في التثبيت أدى إلى إصدار جلسة مسؤول حالية دون التحقق من كلمة المرور. تعمل إصلاحات الأذونات أيضًا على إزالة الوصول العالق لنقل المستودع ومنع مفاتيح النشر من وراثة امتيازات مالك المستودع.

يجب على المسؤولين إجراء نسخ احتياطي للبيانات ومراجعة التغييرات العاجلة والترقية إلى 28.1.0. تشرح ملاحظات إصدار Gitea قواعد الشبكة الجديدة والحد الأدنى لـ Git 2.25 وسلوك سير العمل المتغير.

يوقف التهديدات قبل الاصطدام باستخدام MTTR أسرع بـ 21 دقيقة. قم بدمج Sandbox الخاص بـ ANYRUN في SOC الخاص بك

fr.title: Gitea corrige 27 failles de sécurité, y compris le contournement critique de l'authentification SSH et SSRF
fr.summary: Gitea a publié des mises à jour de sécurité corrigeant 27 failles signalées dans les versions 28.0.0 et 28.1.0, y compris un contournement critique de l'authentification SSH et des faiblesses de falsification de requête côté serveur (SSRF).
fr.content:
Gitea a publié des mises à jour de sécurité corrigeant 27 failles signalées dans les versions 28.0.0 et 28.1.0, y compris un contournement critique de l'authentification SSH et des faiblesses de falsification de requête côté serveur (SSRF).

Les correctifs couvrent l'accès aux comptes, les autorisations du référentiel, les flux de travail automatisés et les connexions aux systèmes internes. Les administrateurs doivent considérer la mise à jour comme une priorité urgente pour leur infrastructure de développement.

Sorti le 30 septembre, Gitea 28.0.0 répertorie 20 CVE dans ses notes de sécurité. Le total signalé de 27 couvre cette version et la mise à jour 28.1.0 qui a suivi, plutôt que la seule version 28.0.0. Gitea a également abandonné son « 1 » historique. préfixe de version, faisant de cette version 28.0.0 au lieu de 1.28.0.

Le problème le plus remarquable, CVE-2026-103059, a un score CVSS de 9,1 et affecte les déploiements utilisant le serveur SSH intégré de Gitea. Sa recherche de clé publique utilisait une comparaison SQL LIKE qui ignore la casse des lettres sur certaines bases de données, y compris la base de données SQLite par défaut. Cela pourrait amener une clé RSA spécialement conçue à correspondre à la clé enregistrée d’un autre utilisateur.

Un attaquant qui construit une variante de cas appropriée de la clé publique d’une victime et en déduit la clé privée correspondante pourrait s’authentifier en tant que victime.

Il ne s’agit pas d’un contournement général utilisant une clé modifiée ; l’attaquant doit répondre à ces exigences clés. Gitea identifie désormais les clés présentées grâce à leurs empreintes digitales, supprimant ainsi la comparaison de texte dangereuse.

## Gitea corrige 27 failles de sécurité

Plusieurs failles corrigées permettaient aux migrations de référentiels et aux miroirs de contourner les règles de connexion sortante. CVE-2026-70357 impliquait un écart entre la validation du nom d'hôte et la connexion Git réelle.

Un attaquant pourrait modifier la réponse DNS du nom d’hôte pendant cet écart, dirigeant Gitea vers un hôte interne une fois le contrôle de sécurité initial réussi.

CVE-2026-101027 permettait à un domaine approuvé d'ignorer les vérifications IP de destination, tandis que CVE-2026-101029 utilisait plusieurs réponses DNS pour contourner la liste autorisée sortante.

Une autre faille, CVE-2026-89430, permet aux miroirs push de se connecter aux hôtes Git internes après que leurs adresses enregistrées ont réussi une vérification antérieure, permettant potentiellement des push forcés.

Gitea achemine désormais les opérations réseau Git via un proxy interne qui applique des règles d'accès sortant lorsque les connexions se produisent. Les administrateurs doivent examiner les modifications de configuration avant la mise à niveau. Pour une politique de refus par défaut, les notes de version demandent aux utilisateurs de définir EGRESS_MODE = strict et de répertorier explicitement les hôtes autorisés.

La mise à jour comble également les lacunes d’approbation de Gitea Actions. CVE-2026-104632 a permis à un workflow fork annulé et en attente d'approbation d'atteindre les exécuteurs auto-hébergés lors de sa réexécution.

CVE-2026-94205 a vérifié uniquement l'acteur de l'événement, permettant à un événement déclenché par le responsable d'exécuter le flux de travail d'un contributeur non fiable sans l'approbation requise. Les deux contrôles sont désormais renforcés.

D'autres correctifs corrigent les scripts intersites stockés dans les blobs de conteneurs, les entrées en double de l'arborescence Git qui pourraient cacher les fichiers malveillants aux réviseurs et une faille d'installation qui émettait une session d'administrateur existante sans vérifier le mot de passe. Les correctifs d'autorisation suppriment également l'accès persistant au transfert de référentiel et empêchent les clés de déploiement d'hériter des privilèges du propriétaire du référentiel.

Les administrateurs doivent sauvegarder les données, examiner les modifications importantes et effectuer la mise à niveau vers la version 28.1.0. Les notes de version de Gitea expliquent les nouvelles règles réseau, Git 2.25 minimum, et le comportement modifié du flux de travail.

de.title: Gitea behebt 27 Sicherheitslücken, einschließlich kritischer Umgehung der SSH-Authentifizierung und SSRF
de.summary: Gitea hat Sicherheitsupdates veröffentlicht, die 27 gemeldete Schwachstellen in den Versionen 28.0.0 und 28.1.0 beheben, darunter eine kritische Umgehung der SSH-Authentifizierung und Schwachstellen bei der serverseitigen Anforderungsfälschung (SSRF).
de.content:
Gitea hat Sicherheitsupdates veröffentlicht, die 27 gemeldete Schwachstellen in den Versionen 28.0.0 und 28.1.0 beheben, darunter eine kritische Umgehung der SSH-Authentifizierung und Schwachstellen bei der serverseitigen Anforderungsfälschung (SSRF).

Die Korrekturen umfassen Kontozugriff, Repository-Berechtigungen, automatisierte Arbeitsabläufe und Verbindungen zu internen Systemen. Administratoren sollten das Update als dringende Priorität für ihre Entwicklungsinfrastruktur betrachten.

Gitea 28.0.0 wurde am 30. September veröffentlicht und listet in seinen Sicherheitshinweisen 20 CVEs auf. Die gemeldete Gesamtzahl von 27 umfasst diese Version und das Folgeupdate 28.1.0 und nicht nur 28.0.0. Gitea ließ auch seine historische „1“ fallen. Versionspräfix, sodass diese Version 28.0.0 anstelle von 1.28.0 ist.

Das herausragende Problem, CVE-2026-103059, hat einen CVSS-Score von 9,1 und betrifft Bereitstellungen, die den integrierten SSH-Server von Gitea verwenden. Bei der Suche nach öffentlichen Schlüsseln wurde ein SQL-LIKE-Vergleich verwendet, der bei einigen Datenbanken, einschließlich der Standard-SQLite-Datenbank, die Groß-/Kleinschreibung ignoriert. Dies könnte dazu führen, dass ein speziell gestalteter RSA-Schlüssel mit dem registrierten Schlüssel eines anderen Benutzers übereinstimmt.

Ein Angreifer, der eine geeignete Fallvariante des öffentlichen Schlüssels eines Opfers erstellt und den dazugehörigen privaten Schlüssel ableitet, könnte sich als dieses Opfer authentifizieren.

Dies ist keine allgemeine Umgehung mit einem geänderten Schlüssel; Der Angreifer muss diese Schlüsselanforderungen erfüllen. Gitea identifiziert präsentierte Schlüssel jetzt anhand ihrer Fingerabdrücke und entfernt so den unsicheren Textvergleich.

## Gitea behebt 27 Sicherheitslücken

Mehrere behobene Schwachstellen ermöglichten es Repository-Migrationen und Spiegelungen, Regeln für ausgehende Verbindungen zu umgehen. CVE-2026-70357 führte zu einer Lücke zwischen der Hostnamen-Validierung und der tatsächlichen Git-Verbindung.

Ein Angreifer könnte während dieser Lücke die DNS-Antwort des Hostnamens ändern und Gitea nach bestandener erster Sicherheitsüberprüfung an einen internen Host weiterleiten.

CVE-2026-101027 erlaubte einer genehmigten Domäne, Ziel-IP-Prüfungen zu überspringen, während CVE-2026-101029 mehrere DNS-Antworten verwendete, um die Outbound-Zulassungsliste zu umgehen.

Ein weiterer Fehler, CVE-2026-89430, ermöglichte es Push-Spiegeln, eine Verbindung zu internen Git-Hosts herzustellen, nachdem ihre gespeicherten Adressen eine frühere Prüfung bestanden hatten, was möglicherweise erzwungene Pushs ermöglichte.

Gitea leitet Git-Netzwerkvorgänge jetzt über einen internen Proxy weiter, der ausgehende Zugriffsregeln anwendet, wenn Verbindungen hergestellt werden. Administratoren müssen Konfigurationsänderungen vor dem Upgrade überprüfen. Für eine Standardverweigerungsrichtlinie werden Benutzer in den Versionshinweisen angewiesen, EGRESS_MODE = strict festzulegen und zulässige Hosts explizit aufzulisten.

Das Update schließt auch Genehmigungslücken bei Gitea Actions. CVE-2026-104632 ermöglichte es einem abgebrochenen, noch nicht genehmigten Fork-Workflow, selbst gehostete Läufer zu erreichen, wenn er erneut ausgeführt wurde.

CVE-2026-94205 überprüfte nur den Ereignisakteur und ermöglichte so einem vom Betreuer ausgelösten Ereignis, den Workflow eines nicht vertrauenswürdigen Mitwirkenden ohne die erforderliche Genehmigung auszuführen. Beide Kontrollen werden nun verschärft.

Andere Korrekturen beheben gespeichertes Cross-Site-Scripting in Container-Blobs, doppelte Git-Baumeinträge, die schädliche Dateien vor Prüfern verbergen könnten, und einen Installationsfehler, der eine bestehende Administratorsitzung ohne Überprüfung des Passworts auslöste. Berechtigungskorrekturen entfernen außerdem den verbleibenden Zugriff auf die Repository-Übertragung und verhindern, dass Bereitstellungsschlüssel die Berechtigungen des Repository-Besitzers erben.

Administratoren sollten Daten sichern, wichtige Änderungen überprüfen und auf 28.1.0 aktualisieren. In den Versionshinweisen von Gitea werden die neuen Netzwerkregeln, mindestens Git 2.25, und das geänderte Workflow-Verhalten erläutert.

es.title: Gitea corrige 27 fallas de seguridad, incluida la omisión de autenticación SSH crítica y SSRF
es.summary: Gitea ha publicado actualizaciones de seguridad que abordan 27 fallas reportadas en las versiones 28.0.0 y 28.1.0, incluida una omisión crítica de autenticación SSH y debilidades de falsificación de solicitudes del lado del servidor (SSRF).
es.content:
Gitea ha publicado actualizaciones de seguridad que abordan 27 fallas reportadas en las versiones 28.0.0 y 28.1.0, incluida una omisión crítica de autenticación SSH y debilidades de falsificación de solicitudes del lado del servidor (SSRF).

Las correcciones cubren el acceso a la cuenta, los permisos del repositorio, los flujos de trabajo automatizados y las conexiones a sistemas internos. Los administradores deben tratar la actualización como una prioridad urgente para su infraestructura de desarrollo.

Lanzado el 30 de septiembre, Gitea 28.0.0 enumera 20 CVE en sus notas de seguridad. El total informado de 27 abarca esa versión y la actualización de seguimiento 28.1.0, en lugar de solo la 28.0.0. Gitea también eliminó su histórico "1". prefijo de versión, lo que hace que esta versión sea 28.0.0 en lugar de 1.28.0.

El problema destacado, CVE-2026-103059, tiene una puntuación CVSS de 9,1 y afecta las implementaciones que utilizan el servidor SSH integrado de Gitea. Su búsqueda de clave pública utilizó una comparación SQL LIKE que ignora las mayúsculas y minúsculas en algunas bases de datos, incluida la base de datos SQLite predeterminada. Esto podría provocar que una clave RSA especialmente diseñada coincida con la clave registrada de otro usuario.

Un atacante que construye una variante de caso adecuada de la clave pública de una víctima y obtiene su clave privada correspondiente podría autenticarse como esa víctima.

Esto no es una omisión general mediante el uso de ninguna clave modificada; el atacante debe cumplir esos requisitos clave. Gitea ahora identifica las claves presentadas a través de sus huellas digitales, eliminando la comparación de texto insegura.

## Gitea parchea 27 fallos de seguridad

Varias fallas parcheadas permitieron que las migraciones de repositorios y las réplicas eludieran las reglas de conexión saliente. CVE-2026-70357 implicó una brecha entre la validación del nombre de host y la conexión Git real.

Un atacante podría cambiar la respuesta DNS del nombre de host durante ese intervalo, dirigiendo a Gitea hacia un host interno después de pasar la verificación de seguridad inicial.

CVE-2026-101027 permitió que un dominio aprobado omitiera las comprobaciones de IP de destino, mientras que CVE-2026-101029 utilizó múltiples respuestas de DNS para omitir la lista de permitidos salientes.

Otra falla, CVE-2026-89430, permitía que los espejos de inserción se conectaran a hosts internos de Git después de que sus direcciones guardadas hubieran pasado una verificación anterior, lo que potencialmente permitía inserciones forzadas.

Gitea ahora enruta las operaciones de red Git a través de un proxy interno que aplica reglas de acceso saliente cuando se producen conexiones. Los administradores deben revisar los cambios de configuración antes de realizar la actualización. Para una política de denegación predeterminada, las notas de la versión indican a los usuarios que establezcan EGRESS_MODE = estricto y enumeren explícitamente los hosts permitidos.

La actualización también cierra las brechas de aprobación de Gitea Actions. CVE-2026-104632 permitió que un flujo de trabajo de bifurcación cancelado y pendiente de aprobación llegara a los ejecutores autohospedados cuando se volviera a ejecutar.

CVE-2026-94205 verificó solo el actor del evento, lo que permite que un evento activado por el mantenedor ejecute el flujo de trabajo de un colaborador que no es de confianza sin la aprobación requerida. Ambos controles ahora son más estrictos.

Otras correcciones abordan secuencias de comandos entre sitios almacenadas en blobs de contenedores, entradas duplicadas del árbol Git que podrían ocultar archivos maliciosos a los revisores y una falla del instalador que generaba una sesión de administrador existente sin verificar la contraseña. Las correcciones de permisos también eliminan el acceso persistente a la transferencia del repositorio y evitan que las claves de implementación hereden los privilegios del propietario del repositorio.

Los administradores deben hacer una copia de seguridad de los datos, revisar los cambios importantes y actualizar a 28.1.0. Las notas de la versión de Gitea explican las nuevas reglas de red, el mínimo de Git 2.25 y el comportamiento modificado del flujo de trabajo.

tr.title: Gitea, Kritik SSH Kimlik Doğrulaması Atlaması ve SSRF dahil 27 Güvenlik Kusurunu Düzeltiyor
tr.summary: Gitea, kritik SSH kimlik doğrulama atlama ve sunucu tarafı istek sahteciliği (SSRF) zayıflıkları da dahil olmak üzere 28.0.0 ve 28.1.0 sürümlerinde bildirilen 27 kusuru ele alan güvenlik güncellemeleri yayınladı.
tr.content:
Gitea, kritik SSH kimlik doğrulama atlama ve sunucu tarafı istek sahteciliği (SSRF) zayıflıkları da dahil olmak üzere 28.0.0 ve 28.1.0 sürümlerinde bildirilen 27 kusuru ele alan güvenlik güncellemeleri yayınladı.

Düzeltmeler hesap erişimini, veri havuzu izinlerini, otomatik iş akışlarını ve dahili sistemlere bağlantıları kapsar. Yöneticiler güncellemeyi geliştirme altyapıları için acil bir öncelik olarak ele almalıdır.

30 Eylül'de yayınlanan Gitea 28.0.0, güvenlik notlarında 20 CVE'yi listeliyor. Yalnızca 28.0.0 yerine, sürüm ve takip eden 28.1.0 güncellemesinin rapor edildiği toplam 27 aralık. Gitea ayrıca tarihi “1” rakamını da düşürdü. sürüm öneki, bu sürümü 1.28.0 yerine 28.0.0 yapıyor.

Öne çıkan sorun olan CVE-2026-103059, CVSS puanı 9,1'dir ve Gitea'nın yerleşik SSH sunucusunu kullanan dağıtımları etkilemektedir. Genel anahtar araması, varsayılan SQLite veritabanı da dahil olmak üzere bazı veritabanlarındaki harf durumunu göz ardı eden bir SQL LIKE karşılaştırması kullandı. Bu, özel hazırlanmış bir RSA anahtarının başka bir kullanıcının kayıtlı anahtarıyla eşleşmesine neden olabilir.

Bir kurbanın genel anahtarının uygun bir durum varyantını oluşturan ve onunla eşleşen özel anahtarı türeten bir saldırgan, kimliğini o kurban olarak doğrulayabilir.

Bu, değiştirilmiş herhangi bir anahtarın kullanıldığı genel bir bypass değildir; saldırganın bu temel gereksinimleri karşılaması gerekir. Gitea artık sunulan anahtarları parmak izleriyle tanımlayarak güvenli olmayan metin karşılaştırmasını ortadan kaldırıyor.

## Gitea 27 Güvenlik Kusurunu Düzeltiyor

Çeşitli yamalı kusurlar, depo geçişlerinin ve aynaların giden bağlantı kurallarını atlamasına izin verdi. CVE-2026-70357, ana bilgisayar adı doğrulaması ile gerçek Git bağlantısı arasında bir boşluk içeriyordu.

Bir saldırgan, bu boşluk sırasında ana bilgisayar adının DNS yanıtını değiştirerek, ilk güvenlik kontrolü geçtikten sonra Gitea'yı dahili bir ana bilgisayara yönlendirebilir.

CVE-2026-101027, onaylanmış bir alanın hedef IP kontrollerini atlamasına izin verirken CVE-2026-101029, giden izin verilenler listesini atlamak için birden fazla DNS yanıtı kullandı.

Başka bir kusur olan CVE-2026-89430, push aynalarının kayıtlı adresleri daha önceki bir kontrolü geçtikten sonra dahili Git ana bilgisayarlarına bağlanmasına izin veriyor ve potansiyel olarak zorla göndermelere izin veriyor.

Gitea artık Git ağ işlemlerini, bağlantı oluştuğunda giden erişim kurallarını uygulayan dahili bir proxy aracılığıyla yönlendiriyor. Yöneticilerin yükseltmeden önce yapılandırma değişikliklerini incelemesi gerekir. Varsayılan olarak reddetme politikası için sürüm notları, kullanıcıları EGRESS_MODE = katı ayarlamaya ve izin verilen ana bilgisayarları açıkça listelemeye yönlendirir.

Güncelleme aynı zamanda Gitea Actions onay boşluklarını da kapatıyor. CVE-2026-104632, iptal edilmiş, onay bekleyen bir çatal iş akışının, yeniden çalıştırıldığında kendi kendine barındırılan koşuculara ulaşmasına izin verdi.

CVE-2026-94205 yalnızca olay aktörünü kontrol ederek bakımcı tarafından tetiklenen bir olayın, güvenilmeyen bir katkıda bulunanın iş akışını gerekli onay olmadan çalıştırmasına izin verdi. Artık her iki denetim de sıkılaştırıldı.

Diğer düzeltmeler, konteyner bloblarında depolanan siteler arası komut dosyalarını, kötü amaçlı dosyaları gözden geçirenlerden gizleyebilecek yinelenen Git ağacı girişlerini ve mevcut bir yöneticinin parolasını kontrol etmeden oturum açmasına neden olan bir yükleyici kusurunu giderir. İzin düzeltmeleri aynı zamanda kalıcı depo aktarım erişimini de ortadan kaldırır ve dağıtım anahtarlarının depo sahibi ayrıcalıklarını devralmasını engeller.

Yöneticiler verileri yedeklemeli, son değişiklikleri gözden geçirmeli ve 28.1.0'a yükseltmelidir. Gitea'nın sürüm notları yeni ağ kurallarını, minimum Git 2.25'i ve değişen iş akışı davranışını açıklıyor.

21 dakika daha hızlı MTTR ile tehditleri etkiden önce durdurur. ANYRUN'un Sandbox'ını SOC'nize entegre edin

Gitea, Kritik SSH Kimlik Doğrulaması Atlaması ve SSRF dahil 27 Güvenlik Kusurunu Yamaladı yazısı ilk olarak Siber Güvenlik Haberlerinde çıktı.

ru.title: Gitea исправляет 27 недостатков безопасности, включая критический обход аутентификации SSH и SSRF
ru.summary: Gitea выпустила обновления безопасности, устраняющие 27 обнаруженных недостатков в версиях 28.0.0 и 28.1.0, включая критический обход аутентификации SSH и уязвимости подделки запросов на стороне сервера (SSRF).
ru.content:
Gitea выпустила обновления безопасности, устраняющие 27 обнаруженных недостатков в версиях 28.0.0 и 28.1.0, включая критический обход аутентификации SSH и уязвимости подделки запросов на стороне сервера (SSRF).

Исправления касаются доступа к учетной записи, разрешений к хранилищу, автоматизированных рабочих процессов и подключений к внутренним системам. Администраторам следует рассматривать обновление как срочный приоритет для своей инфраструктуры развития.

Выпущенная 30 сентября версия Gitea 28.0.0 содержит в примечаниях по безопасности 20 CVE. Сообщается, что в общей сложности 27 охватывают этот выпуск и последующее обновление 28.1.0, а не только 28.0.0. Gitea также отказалась от своей исторической «1». префикс версии, что делает этот выпуск 28.0.0 вместо 1.28.0.

Самая выдающаяся проблема, CVE-2026-103059, имеет оценку CVSS 9,1 и влияет на развертывания с использованием встроенного SSH-сервера Gitea. В его поиске по открытому ключу использовалось сравнение SQL LIKE, которое игнорирует регистр букв в некоторых базах данных, включая базу данных SQLite по умолчанию. Это может привести к тому, что специально созданный ключ RSA будет соответствовать зарегистрированному ключу другого пользователя.

Злоумышленник, создавший подходящий вариант открытого ключа жертвы и получивший соответствующий закрытый ключ, может аутентифицироваться как эта жертва.

Это не общий обход с использованием измененного ключа; злоумышленник должен соответствовать этим ключевым требованиям. Gitea теперь идентифицирует представленные ключи по их отпечаткам пальцев, устраняя небезопасное сравнение текста.

## Gitea исправляет 27 недостатков безопасности

Несколько исправленных ошибок позволяли миграции репозитория и зеркалам обходить правила исходящего соединения. CVE-2026-70357 приводил к разрыву между проверкой имени хоста и фактическим соединением с Git.

Во время этого перерыва злоумышленник может изменить DNS-ответ имени хоста, направив Gitea на внутренний хост после прохождения первоначальной проверки безопасности.

CVE-2026-101027 позволял утвержденному домену пропускать проверки IP-адресов назначения, а CVE-2026-101029 использовал несколько ответов DNS для обхода списка разрешенных исходящих сообщений.

Другая уязвимость, CVE-2026-89430, позволяла push-зеркалам подключаться к внутренним хостам Git после того, как их сохраненные адреса прошли предыдущую проверку, что потенциально допускало принудительные push-уведомления.

Gitea теперь маршрутизирует сетевые операции Git через внутренний прокси-сервер, который применяет правила исходящего доступа при возникновении подключений. Администраторы должны просмотреть изменения конфигурации перед обновлением. Для политики запрета по умолчанию в примечаниях к выпуску пользователям предлагается установить EGRESS_MODE = strict и явно перечислить разрешенные хосты.

Обновление также устраняет пробелы в одобрении Gitea Actions. CVE-2026-104632 позволял отмененному рабочему процессу вилки, ожидающему утверждения, достигать самостоятельных исполнителей при повторном запуске.

CVE-2026-94205 проверял только субъекта события, позволяя событию, инициированному сопровождающим, запускать рабочий процесс ненадежного участника без необходимого одобрения. Обе проверки сейчас ужесточены.

Другие исправления касаются хранящихся межсайтовых сценариев в контейнерных объектах, дублирующих записей дерева Git, которые могут скрыть вредоносные файлы от рецензентов, а также ошибки установщика, из-за которой существующий сеанс администратора запускался без проверки пароля. Исправления разрешений также устраняют устаревший доступ к передаче репозитория и не позволяют ключам развертывания наследовать привилегии владельца репозитория.

Администраторам следует выполнить резервное копирование данных, просмотреть критические изменения и выполнить обновление до версии 28.1.0. В примечаниях к выпуску Gitea объясняются новые сетевые правила, минимум Git 2.25 и измененное поведение рабочего процесса.

Останавливает угрозы до их воздействия благодаря сокращению среднего времени восстановления на 21 минуту. Интегрируйте песочницу ANYRUN в свой SOC

articles.title: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
articles.summary: A new identity theft service launched on the dark web this week is selling digital scans of more than 153 million drivers licenses from people in the United States and Canada. Based on interviews with individuals whose licenses are available for purc
articles.content:
A new identity theft service launched on the dark web this week is selling digital scans of more than 153 million drivers licenses from people in the United States and Canada. Based on interviews with individuals whose licenses are available for purchase on this service, it appears to be siphoning images collected by a widely-used identity verification company based in Louisiana. KrebsOnSecurity also has learned that the New Orleans field office of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) today launched an official inquiry into the source of the images.

A record available at this identity theft service that includes the drivers license for U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, one of several high-ranking U.S. government officials whose drivers licenses can be found for sale.

On Monday, Aug. 31, a source alerted KrebsOnSecurity to a service advertised by a new user on the Russian cybercrime forum Exploit, offering access to digital scans of identity documents on more than 170 million people in North America. The source brought it to my attention because the proprietor of this identity theft service offered my Virginia drivers license as a free sample in their initial sales thread on Exploit.

The service, dubbed Nexus, claims to have more than 153 million drivers licenses for people in the United States and Canada, as well as more than 10 million identification cards; more than three million travel documents and/or international IDs; and at least 579,000 medical cards.

A quick look around Nexus finds they are likely not exaggerating about that 153 million number: Running a blank search in Nexus (with no search parameters entered) returns approximately 11.5 million pages of results, with roughly 15 results displayed per page. It includes documents from people in both Canada and the United States, but the bulk of these records are on Americans: searching for just Canadian drivers licenses returns approximately 1.1 million results, with the largest concentration from Ontario (473,673 records).

Curiously, the identity records include not only drivers licenses but also marijuana dispensary cards. Some of the records list their “source” as “CDL,” presumably short for “commercial drivers license.” Other records carry the source notation of “CAC,” which may refer to Common Access Cards, government issued identity cards that grant physical access to government buildings and secure rooms.

The people behind Nexus claim the license images are coming from an active breach at “a major identity verification company” whose customers include multiple Fortune 500 companies.

The record totals listed by the Nexus identity theft service. The number of drivers license records increased by nearly 400,000 in the span of just 24 hours.

The record featuring my drivers license includes six image files: three pairs of photos of the license’s front and back, a basic image scan, as well as infrared and ultraviolet versions of the same images. Each person whose license could be found (nine of them) confirmed having traveled on or very close to the dates in the timestamps attached to their images. Idscan.net says the company’s systems and technology perform more than 21 million verifications monthly, at more than 20,000 locations around the world.

Contacted by KrebsOnSecurity, idscan.net said it was investigating the matter, but the company has not yet shared an official statement or a substantive reply to specific questions sent via email.

“At this point I’m not able to share any additional information, but the updates you have provided have been welcome, and helpful to our team’s investigation,” wrote Jillian Kossman, a marketing and operations leader at idscan.net.

During the course of my research for this story, word got around to the FBI that I was poking at the apparent source of this new identity theft service’s data. Probably they were tipped off when I shared with a trusted source that Nexus also is selling the drivers license information for the assistant director of the FBI (I did not find FBI Director Kash Patel’s license in Nexus).

Earlier this afternoon, I was added to a conference call with a half-dozen FBI agents, including senior leaders from the agency’s cyber division. During that call, the FBI shared that earlier today their New Orleans field office opened an official investigation into an apparent breach involving idscan.net.

Edwards said that as more in-person and online experiences require sharing drivers licenses, vendors who collect this sensitive data need to be held to a higher standard.

Larry Baldwin is principal intelligence researcher at the cybersecurity firm Cybera. Baldwin said a front and back scan of his drivers license available at Nexus contains timestamps that correspond to the date of a car rental from Hertz on a recent vacation.

This category of people, he said, includes those fleeing domestic violence, and even people who have been assigned a whole new life and identity as part of the federal government’s witness protection program, which is generally reserved for criminal defendants in racketeering and conspiracy investigations who agree to cooperate with federal authorities.

“Just when it seems like we’re making some headway in improving authentication controls through drivers license verification systems, this happens and the very thing those improvements are dependent on are compromised,” Baldwin said.

Update, Sept. 8: IDscan.net published a brief notice saying it has “determined that an unauthorized third party may have accessed and/or copied certain customer information, including full names and drivers license or other government-issued identification numbers.” The statement said IDscan.net is notifying affected individuals and offering credit protection services.

The record featuring my drivers license includes six image files: three pairs of photos of the license’s front and back, a basic image scan, as well as infrared and ultraviolet versions of the same images. Each person whose license could be found (nine of them) confirmed having traveled on or very close to the dates in the timestamps attached to their images. A scan of Edwards’s drivers license is available for purchase on this identity theft service, and Edwards said the timestamp on his record corresponds to the middle of a trip last month to Las Vegas for the annual DEFCON security conference.

Idscan.net says the company’s systems and technology perform more than 21 million verifications monthly, at more than 20,000 locations around the world.

Contacted by KrebsOnSecurity, idscan.net said it was investigating the matter, but the company has not yet shared an official statement or a substantive reply to specific questions sent via email.

“At this point I’m not able to share any additional information, but the updates you have provided have been welcome, and helpful to our team’s investigation,” wrote Jillian Kossman, a marketing and operations leader at idscan.net.

During the course of my research for this story, word got around to the FBI that I was poking at the apparent source of this new identity theft service’s data. Probably they were tipped off when I shared with a trusted source that Nexus also is selling the drivers license information for the assistant director of the FBI (I did not find FBI Director Kash Patel’s license in Nexus).

Earlier this afternoon, I was added to a conference call with a half-dozen FBI agents, including senior leaders from the agency’s cyber division. During that call, the FBI shared that earlier today their New Orleans field office opened an official investigation into an apparent breach involving idscan.net.

Edwards said that as more in-person and online experiences require sharing drivers licenses, vendors who collect this sensitive data need to be held to a higher standard.

This category of people, he said, includes those fleeing domestic violence, and even people who have been assigned a whole new life and identity as part of the federal government’s witness protection program, which is generally reserved for criminal defendants in racketeering and conspiracy investigations who agree to cooperate with federal authorities.

Indeed, over the past 24 hours, the number of drivers license records listed as available in Nexus has increased by nearly 400,000, suggesting that freshly stolen license data is being harvested and uploaded to this service on a semi-regular basis.

The record featuring my drivers license includes six image files: three pairs of photos of the license’s front and back, a basic image scan, as well as infrared and ultraviolet versions of the same images. A date and timestamp is appended to each image file, and the timestamp on my license scan corresponds to a date in June 2025 when I took a flight to the midwest United States to attend a family funeral.

Some of the 153 million+ license scans — including mine — feature six image files with date and timestamps appended to the filenames. Not all records include photos, and some that do feature photos do not display the associated filenames.

Intent on discovering the source of this data, KrebsOnSecurity asked more than a dozen friends and family members for permission to search for their licenses in this service. Each person whose license could be found (nine of them) confirmed having traveled on or very close to the dates in the timestamps attached to their images. It is unclear what timezone these timestamps are in, but from reviewing car rental records shared by several people who helped with this research, it appears the timezone is set to Greenwich Mean Time (GMT).

At first, I thought the source of the data might have something to do with airports. However, that theory went out the window when it became apparent there were no passports in this data set. Also, only some of those who helped with this research said they showed their drivers license at the airport on the day of their travel. One person whose license was in Nexus hadn’t flown at all recently, but was renting a car from Hertz for several months around the date of their timestamp.

Two of those who agreed to help are federal employees who said they shared other forms of government identification when passing through airport security. However, those individuals each said they shared their state-issued drivers licenses later that day when renting vehicles at their respective destinations, and that both rented their cars from Hertz.

After finding a note in my calendar for the day of my June 2025 flight reminding me to bring my passport, I remembered that I also never actually shared my drivers license when I went through security at Reagan National Airport on that day because I did not yet have a Real ID, a security-enhanced drivers license that is now required by the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) for all domestic travel. Instead, I showed the TSA agent my government-issued U.S. passport.

Here’s where it gets interesting: I was able to find my mother’s drivers license in this service as well, and the timestamps for her images are just a few seconds apart from mine. That’s notable because we both handed our licenses to the Hertz rental car representative at the same time.

According to my mom, the only place she gave her drivers license to that day was the rental car company, and if memory serves that is also true for me. I don’t recall if the rental car representative inserted our licenses into any kind of machine, but I remember they held onto them for several minutes behind the counter while we were signing various forms. KrebsOnSecurity sought comment from Hertz and will update this story in the event they reply.

Zach Edwards is a well-known security and privacy researcher who recently launched a service called DecryptAds to help people better understand how online advertisers are tracking them. A scan of Edwards’s drivers license is available for purchase on this identity theft service, and Edwards said the timestamp on his record corresponds to the middle of a trip last month to Las Vegas for the annual DEFCON security conference.

Edwards told KrebsOnSecurity that although he did not rent a car in Vegas, he did hand over his license at the TSA checkpoint, at a marijuana dispensary in Vegas, and at his hotel (the Aria). But he said the only one of those three that for sure scanned his ID in some kind of device was the dispensary.

To enter Planet13’s weed dispensary in Las Vegas, one must pass through a red telephone booth. Image: Zach Edwards.

Edwards said the dispensary he visited that day was Planet13, a multi-state chain with stores in California, Florida, Illinois and Nevada. In 2022, the New Orleans-based identity provider idscan.net published a press release announcing an exclusive identity verification agreement with Planet13’s dispensaries nationally. IDScan says it processes ID verification for more than 1,000 marijuana dispensaries in 19 U.S. states.

The “trust” page of idscan.net states that the company provides identity verification services for numerous big brands, including Hertz, Target, Fedex, Motorola Solutions, the financial services giant Jack Henry, and Caesars Entertainment. And as idscan.net’s own documentation states, the technology scans IDs with both infrared and ultraviolet light. Idscan.net says the company’s systems and technology perform more than 21 million verifications monthly, at more than 20,000 locations around the world.

Contacted by KrebsOnSecurity, idscan.net said it was investigating the matter, but the company has not yet shared an official statement or a substantive reply to specific questions sent via email.

“At this point I’m not able to share any additional information, but the updates you have provided have been welcome, and helpful to our team’s investigation,” wrote Jillian Kossman, a marketing and operations leader at idscan.net.

During the course of my research for this story, word got around to the FBI that I was poking at the apparent source of this new identity theft service’s data. Probably they were tipped off when I shared with a trusted source that Nexus also is selling the drivers license information for the assistant director of the FBI (I did not find FBI Director Kash Patel’s license in Nexus).

Earlier this afternoon, I was added to a conference call with a half-dozen FBI agents, including senior leaders from the agency’s cyber division. During that call, the FBI shared that earlier today their New Orleans field office opened an official investigation into an apparent breach involving idscan.net.

Edwards said that as more in-person and online experiences require sharing drivers licenses, vendors who collect this sensitive data need to be held to a higher standard.

“This episode should further strengthen the resolve for people who are fighting back against online ID schemes which are requiring countless providers to ask for drivers licenses in order to access services under the guise of protecting kids,” Edwards told KrebsOnSecurity. “These systems are putting sensitive data into more and more 3rd party vendors, and we don’t have nearly the oversight to ensure they are safe.”

Larry Baldwin is principal intelligence researcher at the cybersecurity firm Cybera. Baldwin said a front and back scan of his drivers license available at Nexus contains timestamps that correspond to the date of a car rental from Hertz on a recent vacation.

Baldwin said the Nexus identity theft service presents multiple serious security and privacy threats, noting that state-issued drivers licenses are commonly used as proof of one’s identity when opening new lines of credit. Baldwin said the service could also dangerously expose many people who do not wish to be found but who cannot meaningfully change their appearance (or at least not enough to fool today’s AI-based image matching tools).

This category of people, he said, includes those fleeing domestic violence, and even people who have been assigned a whole new life and identity as part of the federal government’s witness protection program, which is generally reserved for criminal defendants in racketeering and conspiracy investigations who agree to cooperate with federal authorities.

“Just when it seems like we’re making some headway in improving authentication controls through drivers license verification systems, this happens and the very thing those improvements are dependent on are compromised,” Baldwin said.

Update, Sept. 8: IDscan.net published a brief notice saying it has “determined that an unauthorized third party may have accessed and/or copied certain customer information, including full names and drivers license or other government-issued identification numbers.” The statement said IDscan.net is notifying affected individuals and offering credit protection services.

Update, Sept. 2, 6:05 p.m. ET: A spokesperson for Caesars Entertainment said Caesars has not been a client of IDScan.net and has not used VeriScan since February 2025, despite IDScan.net listing them as a client on their website. That person said Caesars had no active VeriScan accounts at the time of the incident and did not authorize IDScan.net to retain data from its accounts, and that IDScan.net said the incident should have no impact on Caesars Entertainment.

Update, 8:56 p.m. ET: Shortly after this story was published, the Nexus identity theft service website vanished from the darkweb, replacing its login page with a plain text message that reads, “This service is no longer available.”

This is a potentially fast-moving story. Any changes or updates will be noted here along with a timestamp.

articles.title: Google Pauses Open-Source Bug Bounty Program After Flood of Invalid AI-Generated Reports
articles.summary: Google has temporarily stopped accepting new product vulnerability reports through its Open Source Software Vulnerability Reward Program(OSS VRP) following a major increase in automated submissions that were mostly invalid.
articles.content:
Google has temporarily stopped accepting new product vulnerability reports through its Open Source Software Vulnerability Reward Program(OSS VRP) following a major increase in automated submissions that were mostly invalid.

The change took effect on October 1, 2026, and Google said it will provide an update on the program in the first quarter of 2027.

The decision does not shut down the entire open-source bug bounty program. Supply-chain vulnerability reports remain in scope, and Google will continue handling product vulnerability reports submitted before October 1.

Some vulnerabilities in Google Cloud repositories may also still be accepted through the separate Google Cloud Vulnerability Reward Program. Google said the pause stemmed from a “significant rise” in automated reports, with the vast majority failing validation.

AI-generated submissions can appear technically convincing while containing invented exploit paths, incorrect assumptions about source code behavior, or claims that a vulnerable function is reachable when it is not. This creates a large triage burden for security engineers and open-source maintainers.

The company had already warned researchers about this problem in earlier OSS VRP rule updates. Google identified AI-generated reports containing incorrect triggering conditions and “hallucinations” about how a vulnerability could be exploited.

The program also tightened evidence requirements for certain reports, particularly memory corruption flaws in high-priority projects.

## Google Pauses Open-Source Bug Bounty Program

Google’s OSS VRP covers the latest versions of open-source projects maintained in public repositories owned by Google organizations. It includes issues affecting code, repository settings, GitHub Actions workflows, access controls, build systems, release environments, package publication credentials, and cryptographic signing keys.

The highest-value category remains supply-chain compromise. Researchers can report flaws that could allow an attacker to modify source code, tamper with build artifacts, compromise packages distributed through registries, or abuse build and release infrastructure. Such reports must show a realistic, exploitable path rather than a theoretical risk.

For flagship OT0 projects, supply-chain rewards can range from $3,133.7 to $31,337. Important OT1 projects may receive between $1,337 and $13,337, while standard OT2 projects can qualify for $500 to $3,133.7.

Google does not offer financial rewards for low-priority OT3 repositories. Reward amounts remain subject to the company’s security-impact review.

The paused category is specifically product vulnerabilities. These include software weaknesses such as memory corruption in parsers or network implementations, path traversal flaws, sanitizer failures, and insecure defaults that could substantially affect the confidentiality or integrity of user data in applications built with Google open-source code.

Google’s move highlights a growing problem across vulnerability disclosure programs. Generative AI can help researchers review code, write proof-of-concept material, and identify suspicious patterns.

However, reports still require manual validation, reproducible steps, realistic impact analysis, affected version details, and a clear attack scenario.

Researchers should avoid submitting AI-written findings without verifying them against a recent build. A quality report should include a buildable proof of concept, exact reproduction instructions, crash data where available, evidence that the issue is reachable, and a clear explanation of security impact.

Google is directing researchers toward its other VRP programs and its Patch Rewards Program. At the same time, it is redesigning the paused OSS product-vulnerability intake.

articles.title: Hackers Abuse Legitimate ScreenConnect Tool to Gain Remote Access Through Phishing
articles.summary: Hackers are using a legitimate ScreenConnect client to turn a payment notification into a route for remote access. Instead of delivering custom malware, the phishing attempt directs recipients to software already designed to let someone else connect
articles.content:
Hackers are using a legitimate ScreenConnect client to turn a payment notification into a route for remote access. Instead of delivering custom malware, the phishing attempt directs recipients to software already designed to let someone else connect to their computer.

The email claims that a payment of $5745.65 has been received and invites the recipient to view order information as a PDF.

This resembles earlier remote access phishing lures that disguise administrative software as everyday documents or familiar workplace downloads. Researchers from Internet Storm Center identified the abuse after examining the downloaded program.

Internet Storm Center said in a report shared with Cyber Security News (CSN) that the file was a legitimate client configured to contact an attacker-operated test account.

Published on October 1, 2026, the analysis by Xavier Mertens describes an observed phishing attempt, not a confirmed large-scale breach.

It provides no victim count or evidence of stolen data, but highlights how legitimate remote support software can become an entry point when attackers control its configuration.

## Hackers Abuse Legitimate ScreenConnect Tool

The message uses a wire transfer subject and a paid invoice receipt format to make the request look routine. It also offers cancellation and an immediate refund if the charge was unauthorized, giving recipients another reason to investigate an unexpected transaction.

The central deception is straightforward: the promised PDF is actually a Windows executable. Following the link downloads a ScreenConnect installer rather than the advertised order document. The attack therefore depends on persuading a recipient to run software delivered through an unsolicited financial message.

Mertens reported that the email passed basic security controls. He also noted that browsers would block this delivery approach because downloading an executable is suspicious.

The report does not establish that a recipient bypassed that protection or successfully installed the client on a victim system.

The technique echoes legitimate RMM phishing campaigns that use trusted remote management applications instead of a recognizable malicious payload.

However, the ISC report does not connect this particular email to those operations or attribute it to a named threat group. The downloaded file was unknown on VirusTotal when Mertens examined it.

His analysis found a preconfigured connection to a specific cloud-hosted ScreenConnect instance, using port 443. That configuration would direct the client toward the attacker’s account rather than an organization’s approved support environment.

## Detection Challenges

The executable carried a digital signature from ConnectWise, LLC, issued through DigiCert G4 Code Signing CA1. Its Authenticode digest matched the signed digest exactly, meaning the checked file content corresponded to what the publisher had signed.

Mertens also found no extra data appended to the executable and no additions or injections in its certificate table. He explicitly ruled out a signed-but-tampered configuration trick.

The finding matters because the suspicious behavior came from the software’s intended remote access function, not an altered binary. The case illustrates a gap between identifying a program and deciding whether its use is actually safe.

Here, the software was genuine, but the email misrepresented what the recipient would receive. The relevant question is who arranged the installation and which remote account the client is configured to ultimately reach after it starts.

For defenders, that distinction changes the investigation. Earlier reporting on detecting trusted tool abuse explains why download context, user expectations, execution activity, and subsequent connections matter together.

A legitimate installer does not, by itself, prove that the resulting remote session was authorized. The ISC report points readers to the LOLRMM project for a broader inventory of remote management tools that attackers can misuse.

Its wider message is that familiar support applications deserve scrutiny when their installation follows an unexpected email rather than a verified support request.

The indicators below come from the ISC report, not the separate campaigns linked for context. The published key hash is abbreviated, so it cannot serve as a complete SHA-256 matching value.

The relay is legitimate cloud infrastructure associated with the observed configuration, not evidence that every ScreenConnect connection is malicious.

articles.title: Vercel Confirms KVM Zero-Day VM Escape, Awards Researcher $50,000
articles.summary: Vercel has confirmed a KVM zero-day vulnerability after security researcher Paulos Yibelo reported a full virtual machine escape that, he says, allows code inside a guest to gain root access on the host.
articles.content:
Vercel has confirmed a KVM zero-day vulnerability after security researcher Paulos Yibelo reported a full virtual machine escape that, he says, allows code inside a guest to gain root access on the host.

The discovery came through the Vercel Sandbox bug bounty program, raising concerns about a security boundary used to contain untrusted workloads and AI agents.

Yibelo announced the finding on October 3, 2026, describing it as a “Full VM escape zeroday” involving “guest>host root” in industry-standard hypervisors. Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch separately confirmed a KVM zero-day and said a full technical write-up would follow. Neither statement explained the exploit chain or identified affected versions.

## KVM Zero-Day VM Escape

A bounty notification shared with the announcement shows Vercel awarding Yibelo $50,000, the program’s maximum payment for one report. The message describes the highest award as reserved for vulnerabilities that let an attacker read or change another Vercel customer’s information. Its critical category includes microVM escapes to an EC2 host and access to another customer’s data or code execution.

However, that award description should not be treated as a public demonstration of customer data theft. The screenshot hides the report’s root cause, and the available statements do not establish that real customer information was accessed.

Vercel’s $1 million Sandbox challenge opened on August 18, 2026, with a scheduled closing date of September 1. Its published rules require a live proof of concept showing a broken security boundary, rather than a report based only on reviewing code.

KVM, short for Kernel-based Virtual Machine, provides Linux virtualization. A guest virtual machine should remain separate from the host that runs it. A successful guest-to-host escape breaks that separation; root access gives an attacker the highest level of control on the host.

Vercel’s published architecture places each sandbox inside its own Firecracker microVM on a bare-metal Amazon EC2 host. Each microVM has a dedicated guest kernel, while a Linux container inside it runs the user’s code. Vercel explicitly identifies the microVM, not the container, as the main security boundary.

This distinction matters for AI agents that execute generated or downloaded code. Moving from a container into its guest operating system is not the same as reaching the underlying host. Yibelo’s claim describes the more serious boundary crossing, although the exact technical steps remain undisclosed.

The announcement does not identify a CVE, affected kernel releases, processor requirements, or a patch. It also does not establish whether guest administrator access is required. Rauch’s reference to KVM does not prove that every KVM deployment, Firecracker installation, or cloud provider is vulnerable. The missing details also prevent an independent assessment of exploit reliability across different host configurations.

For background, Cybersecuritynews previously covered the separate Januscape KVM vulnerability, which involved host memory corruption through nested virtualization. There is no disclosed evidence linking that issue to Yibelo’s finding, so its exploit conditions and fixes should not be applied to this report.

Until the technical disclosure arrives, operators should follow Vercel and their Linux vendors for guidance, rather than assume an unrelated patch addresses this flaw. The immediate takeaway is a confirmed vulnerability report and a claimed host-root escape, not confirmed widespread exploitation.

The promised write-up should clarify the root cause, affected systems, and available protections, allowing defenders to assess exposure without guessing. Those details will determine which deployments actually need urgent action.

ar.title: Vercel تؤكد KVM Zero-Day VM Escape، وتمنح الباحث جائزة قدرها 50000 دولار
ar.summary: أكد Vercel وجود ثغرة أمنية في KVM بعد أن أبلغ الباحث الأمني ​​Paulos Yibelo عن هروب كامل للجهاز الظاهري، والذي، كما يقول، يسمح للكود الموجود داخل الضيف بالوصول إلى الجذر على المضيف.
ar.content:
أكد Vercel وجود ثغرة أمنية في KVM بعد أن أبلغ الباحث الأمني ​​Paulos Yibelo عن هروب كامل للجهاز الظاهري، والذي، كما يقول، يسمح للكود الموجود داخل الضيف بالوصول إلى الجذر على المضيف.

جاء هذا الاكتشاف من خلال برنامج مكافآت الأخطاء Vercel Sandbox، مما أثار مخاوف بشأن الحدود الأمنية المستخدمة لاحتواء أعباء العمل غير الموثوق بها ووكلاء الذكاء الاصطناعي.

أعلن Yibelo عن النتيجة في 3 أكتوبر 2026، واصفًا إياها بأنها "عملية هروب كاملة من الأجهزة الافتراضية" تتضمن "جذر الضيف> المضيف" في برامج Hypervisor المتوافقة مع معايير الصناعة. أكد الرئيس التنفيذي لشركة Vercel Guillermo Rauch بشكل منفصل وجود يوم صفر لـ KVM وقال إن الكتابة الفنية الكاملة ستتبع. ولم يوضح أي من البيانين سلسلة الاستغلال أو الإصدارات المتأثرة المحددة.

## KVM Zero-Day VM Escape

يُظهر إشعار المكافأة الذي تمت مشاركته مع الإعلان أن شركة Vercel تمنح Yibelo مبلغ 50000 دولار، وهو الحد الأقصى للدفع للبرنامج مقابل تقرير واحد. تصف الرسالة أعلى جائزة بأنها مخصصة للثغرات الأمنية التي تسمح للمهاجم بقراءة معلومات عميل Vercel آخر أو تغييرها. تتضمن فئتها المهمة عمليات هروب microVM إلى مضيف EC2 والوصول إلى بيانات عميل آخر أو تنفيذ التعليمات البرمجية.

ومع ذلك، لا ينبغي التعامل مع هذا الوصف للجائزة كدليل عام على سرقة بيانات العميل. تخفي لقطة الشاشة السبب الجذري للتقرير، ولا تثبت البيانات المتاحة أنه تم الوصول إلى معلومات العميل الحقيقية.

تم افتتاح تحدي Sandbox الذي تبلغ تكلفته مليون دولار من شركة Vercel في 18 أغسطس 2026، مع تاريخ إغلاق مقرر هو 1 سبتمبر. وتتطلب قواعدها المنشورة إثباتًا حيًا للمفهوم يظهر حدودًا أمنية مكسورة، بدلاً من تقرير يعتمد فقط على مراجعة التعليمات البرمجية.

توفر KVM، وهي اختصار لـ Virtual Machine المستندة إلى Kernel، محاكاة Linux الافتراضية. يجب أن يظل الجهاز الظاهري الضيف منفصلاً عن المضيف الذي يقوم بتشغيله. يكسر الهروب الناجح من الضيف إلى المضيف هذا الانفصال؛ يمنح الوصول إلى الجذر المهاجم أعلى مستوى من التحكم في المضيف.

تضع بنية Vercel المنشورة كل صندوق حماية داخل جهاز Firecracker microVM الخاص به على مضيف Amazon EC2 المعدني. يحتوي كل جهاز microVM على نواة ضيف مخصصة، بينما تقوم حاوية Linux بداخله بتشغيل كود المستخدم. يحدد Vercel بشكل صريح microVM، وليس الحاوية، كحدود الأمان الرئيسية.

هذا التمييز مهم بالنسبة لوكلاء الذكاء الاصطناعي الذين ينفذون التعليمات البرمجية التي تم إنشاؤها أو تنزيلها. إن الانتقال من الحاوية إلى نظام التشغيل الضيف الخاص بها لا يماثل الوصول إلى المضيف الأساسي. يصف ادعاء يبيلو المعبر الحدودي الأكثر خطورة، على الرغم من أن الخطوات الفنية الدقيقة لم يتم الكشف عنها بعد.

لا يحدد الإعلان CVE، أو إصدارات kernel المتأثرة، أو متطلبات المعالج، أو التصحيح. كما أنه لا يحدد ما إذا كان وصول المسؤول الضيف مطلوبًا أم لا. لا تثبت إشارة Rauch إلى KVM أن كل عملية نشر لـ KVM، أو تثبيت Firecracker، أو موفر السحابة معرضة للخطر. تمنع التفاصيل المفقودة أيضًا إجراء تقييم مستقل لموثوقية استغلال الثغرات عبر تكوينات المضيف المختلفة.

للحصول على معلومات أساسية، غطت Cybersecuritynews سابقًا ثغرة Januscape KVM المنفصلة، ​​والتي تضمنت تلف ذاكرة المضيف من خلال المحاكاة الافتراضية المتداخلة. لا يوجد دليل مُفصح عنه يربط هذه المشكلة باكتشافات Yibelo، لذا لا ينبغي تطبيق شروط الاستغلال وإصلاحاته على هذا التقرير.

وإلى أن يصل الكشف الفني، يجب على المشغلين اتباع شركة Vercel وموردي Linux للحصول على إرشادات، بدلاً من افتراض وجود تصحيح غير ذي صلة يعالج هذا الخلل. النتيجة المباشرة هي تقرير ثغرة أمنية مؤكدة وهروب جذر المضيف المزعوم، وليس استغلالًا مؤكدًا على نطاق واسع.

يجب أن توضح الكتابة الموعودة السبب الجذري، والأنظمة المتأثرة، ووسائل الحماية المتاحة، مما يسمح للمدافعين بتقييم التعرض دون التخمين. ستحدد هذه التفاصيل عمليات النشر التي تحتاج بالفعل إلى إجراء عاجل.

fr.title: Vercel confirme l'évasion KVM Zero-Day VM et récompense le chercheur 50 000 $
fr.summary: Vercel a confirmé une vulnérabilité KVM Zero Day après que le chercheur en sécurité Paulos Yibelo a signalé une évasion complète de la machine virtuelle qui, dit-il, permet au code interne d'un invité d'obtenir un accès root sur l'hôte.
fr.content:
Vercel a confirmé une vulnérabilité KVM Zero Day après que le chercheur en sécurité Paulos Yibelo a signalé une évasion complète de la machine virtuelle qui, dit-il, permet au code interne d'un invité d'obtenir un accès root sur l'hôte.

La découverte a eu lieu grâce au programme Vercel Sandbox Bug Bounty, soulevant des inquiétudes concernant une limite de sécurité utilisée pour contenir des charges de travail et des agents d'IA non fiables.

Yibelo a annoncé la découverte le 3 octobre 2026, la décrivant comme une « évasion complète de la VM zeroday » impliquant « invité> racine hôte » dans les hyperviseurs standard de l'industrie. Le PDG de Vercel, Guillermo Rauch, a confirmé séparément un KVM zero-day et a déclaré qu'un rapport technique complet suivrait. Aucune des deux déclarations n'expliquait la chaîne d'exploitation ou n'identifiait les versions affectées.

## Évasion de VM KVM Zero-Day

Une notification de prime partagée avec l'annonce montre que Vercel accorde à Yibelo 50 000 $, le paiement maximum du programme pour un rapport. Le message décrit la récompense la plus élevée comme étant réservée aux vulnérabilités permettant à un attaquant de lire ou de modifier les informations d'un autre client Vercel. Sa catégorie critique comprend les fuites de microVM vers un hôte EC2 et l’accès aux données ou à l’exécution de code d’un autre client.

Cependant, cette description de récompense ne doit pas être considérée comme une démonstration publique de vol de données client. La capture d’écran masque la cause première du rapport et les déclarations disponibles n’établissent pas que de véritables informations client ont été consultées.

Le défi Sandbox d'un million de dollars de Vercel a débuté le 18 août 2026, avec une date de clôture prévue le 1er septembre. Ses règles publiées exigent une preuve de concept en direct montrant une frontière de sécurité brisée, plutôt qu'un rapport basé uniquement sur la révision du code.

KVM, abréviation de Kernel-based Virtual Machine, fournit la virtualisation Linux. Une machine virtuelle invitée doit rester distincte de l'hôte qui l'exécute. Une évasion réussie entre hôte et invité brise cette séparation ; L'accès root donne à un attaquant le plus haut niveau de contrôle sur l'hôte.

L'architecture publiée par Vercel place chaque bac à sable dans sa propre microVM Firecracker sur un hôte Amazon EC2 nu. Chaque microVM possède un noyau invité dédié, tandis qu'un conteneur Linux à l'intérieur exécute le code de l'utilisateur. Vercel identifie explicitement la microVM, et non le conteneur, comme principale limite de sécurité.

Cette distinction est importante pour les agents IA qui exécutent du code généré ou téléchargé. Passer d'un conteneur à son système d'exploitation invité n'est pas la même chose que d'atteindre l'hôte sous-jacent. L’affirmation de Yibelo décrit le franchissement de la frontière le plus grave, bien que les étapes techniques exactes ne soient pas divulguées.

L'annonce n'identifie pas de CVE, les versions du noyau concernées, les exigences du processeur ou un correctif. Il n'établit pas non plus si un accès administrateur invité est requis. La référence de Rauch à KVM ne prouve pas que chaque déploiement KVM, installation Firecracker ou fournisseur de cloud est vulnérable. Les détails manquants empêchent également une évaluation indépendante de la fiabilité des exploits sur différentes configurations d’hôtes.

Pour information, Cybersecuritynews a déjà couvert la vulnérabilité distincte de Januscape KVM, qui impliquait une corruption de la mémoire hôte via une virtualisation imbriquée. Aucune preuve n’a été divulguée liant ce problème aux conclusions de Yibelo, ses conditions d’exploitation et ses correctifs ne doivent donc pas être appliqués à ce rapport.

En attendant la divulgation technique, les opérateurs devraient suivre Vercel et leurs fournisseurs Linux pour obtenir des conseils, plutôt que de supposer qu'un correctif sans rapport corrige cette faille. Ce qu'il faut retenir immédiatement, c'est un rapport de vulnérabilité confirmé et une prétendue évasion de la racine de l'hôte, mais une exploitation généralisée non confirmée.

Le texte promis devrait clarifier la cause profonde, les systèmes concernés et les protections disponibles, permettant aux défenseurs d'évaluer l'exposition sans deviner. Ces détails détermineront quels déploiements nécessitent réellement une action urgente.

de.title: Vercel bestätigt KVM-Zero-Day-VM-Flucht und belohnt Forscher mit 50.000 US-Dollar
de.summary: Vercel hat eine KVM-Zero-Day-Schwachstelle bestätigt, nachdem der Sicherheitsforscher Paulos Yibelo einen vollständigen Escape-Vorgang einer virtuellen Maschine gemeldet hatte, der seiner Aussage zufolge Code in einem Gast ermöglicht, Root-Zugriff auf den Host zu erhalten.
de.content:
Vercel hat eine KVM-Zero-Day-Schwachstelle bestätigt, nachdem der Sicherheitsforscher Paulos Yibelo einen vollständigen Escape-Vorgang einer virtuellen Maschine gemeldet hatte, der seiner Aussage zufolge Code in einem Gast ermöglicht, Root-Zugriff auf den Host zu erhalten.

Die Entdeckung erfolgte durch das Bug-Bounty-Programm Vercel Sandbox und gab Anlass zu Bedenken hinsichtlich einer Sicherheitsgrenze, die zur Eindämmung nicht vertrauenswürdiger Workloads und KI-Agenten verwendet wurde.

Yibelo gab das Ergebnis am 3. Oktober 2026 bekannt und beschrieb es als „vollständigen VM-Escape-Zeroday“, der „Gast>Host-Root“ in branchenüblichen Hypervisoren beinhaltet. Guillermo Rauch, CEO von Vercel, bestätigte separat einen KVM-Zero-Day und sagte, eine vollständige technische Beschreibung werde folgen. Keine der Aussagen erläuterte die Exploit-Kette oder identifizierte betroffene Versionen.

## KVM Zero-Day VM Escape

Eine mit der Ankündigung geteilte Kopfgeldbenachrichtigung zeigt, dass Vercel Yibelo 50.000 US-Dollar zuspricht, die maximale Zahlung des Programms für einen Bericht. In der Nachricht wird beschrieben, dass die höchste Auszeichnung Schwachstellen vorbehalten ist, die es einem Angreifer ermöglichen, die Informationen eines anderen Vercel-Kunden zu lesen oder zu ändern. Zu seiner kritischen Kategorie gehören MicroVM-Escapes zu einem EC2-Host und Zugriff auf die Daten oder Codeausführung eines anderen Kunden.

Diese Prämienbeschreibung sollte jedoch nicht als öffentliche Demonstration des Diebstahls von Kundendaten angesehen werden. Der Screenshot verschleiert die Ursache des Berichts und die verfügbaren Aussagen belegen nicht, dass auf echte Kundeninformationen zugegriffen wurde.

Vercels 1-Millionen-Dollar-Sandbox-Challenge wurde am 18. August 2026 eröffnet und endet am 1. September. Die veröffentlichten Regeln erfordern einen Live-Proof of Concept, der eine durchbrochene Sicherheitsgrenze zeigt, und keinen Bericht, der nur auf der Überprüfung von Code basiert.

KVM, kurz für Kernel-based Virtual Machine, bietet Linux-Virtualisierung. Eine virtuelle Gastmaschine sollte vom Host, auf dem sie ausgeführt wird, getrennt bleiben. Eine erfolgreiche Flucht zwischen Gast und Gastgeber durchbricht diese Trennung; Root-Zugriff gibt einem Angreifer das höchste Maß an Kontrolle über den Host.

Die veröffentlichte Architektur von Vercel platziert jede Sandbox in ihrer eigenen Firecracker-MicroVM auf einem Bare-Metal-Amazon EC2-Host. Jede microVM verfügt über einen dedizierten Gastkernel, während ein darin enthaltener Linux-Container den Code des Benutzers ausführt. Vercel identifiziert explizit die microVM und nicht den Container als Hauptsicherheitsgrenze.

Diese Unterscheidung ist für KI-Agenten wichtig, die generierten oder heruntergeladenen Code ausführen. Der Wechsel von einem Container in sein Gastbetriebssystem ist nicht dasselbe wie das Erreichen des zugrunde liegenden Hosts. Yibelos Behauptung beschreibt die schwerwiegendere Grenzüberschreitung, obwohl die genauen technischen Schritte nicht bekannt gegeben werden.

In der Ankündigung werden kein CVE, betroffene Kernel-Releases, Prozessoranforderungen oder ein Patch genannt. Es wird auch nicht festgestellt, ob Gastadministratorzugriff erforderlich ist. Rauchs Verweis auf KVM beweist nicht, dass jede KVM-Bereitstellung, Firecracker-Installation oder jeder Cloud-Anbieter angreifbar ist. Die fehlenden Details verhindern auch eine unabhängige Bewertung der Exploit-Zuverlässigkeit über verschiedene Hostkonfigurationen hinweg.

Als Hintergrundinformationen berichtete Cybersecuritynews zuvor über die separate Januscape-KVM-Schwachstelle, die eine Beschädigung des Hostspeichers durch verschachtelte Virtualisierung zur Folge hatte. Es gibt keine offengelegten Beweise, die dieses Problem mit Yibelos Erkenntnissen in Verbindung bringen, daher sollten die Exploit-Bedingungen und Korrekturen nicht auf diesen Bericht angewendet werden.

Bis die technische Offenlegung vorliegt, sollten sich Betreiber an Vercel und ihre Linux-Anbieter orientieren und nicht davon ausgehen, dass ein unabhängiger Patch diesen Fehler behebt. Die unmittelbare Erkenntnis ist ein bestätigter Schwachstellenbericht und ein angeblicher Host-Root-Fluchtversuch, nicht jedoch eine bestätigte weit verbreitete Ausnutzung.

Der versprochene Bericht soll die Grundursache, die betroffenen Systeme und die verfügbaren Schutzmaßnahmen klären und es den Verteidigern ermöglichen, die Gefährdung ohne Vermutungen einzuschätzen. Anhand dieser Details lässt sich bestimmen, bei welchen Einsätzen tatsächlich dringend gehandelt werden muss.

es.title: Vercel confirma el escape de VM de día cero de KVM y otorga al investigador 50 000 dólares
es.summary: Vercel confirmó una vulnerabilidad de día cero de KVM después de que el investigador de seguridad Paulos Yibelo informara sobre un escape completo de una máquina virtual que, según él, permite que el código dentro de un invitado obtenga acceso raíz en el host.
es.content:
Vercel confirmó una vulnerabilidad de día cero de KVM después de que el investigador de seguridad Paulos Yibelo informara sobre un escape completo de una máquina virtual que, según él, permite que el código dentro de un invitado obtenga acceso raíz en el host.

El descubrimiento se produjo a través del programa de recompensas por errores Vercel Sandbox, lo que generó preocupaciones sobre un límite de seguridad utilizado para contener cargas de trabajo y agentes de inteligencia artificial que no son de confianza.

Yibelo anunció el hallazgo el 3 de octubre de 2026, describiéndolo como un “día cero de escape completo de VM” que involucra “invitado>raíz de host” en hipervisores estándar de la industria. El director general de Vercel, Guillermo Rauch, confirmó por separado un KVM de día cero y dijo que a continuación se realizaría un informe técnico completo. Ninguna declaración explicó la cadena de exploits ni identificó las versiones afectadas.

## Escape de VM de día cero KVM

Una notificación de recompensa compartida con el anuncio muestra que Vercel otorga a Yibelo 50.000 dólares, el pago máximo del programa por un informe. El mensaje describe el premio más alto como reservado para vulnerabilidades que permiten a un atacante leer o cambiar la información de otro cliente de Vercel. Su categoría crítica incluye escapes de microVM a un host EC2 y acceso a los datos o la ejecución de código de otro cliente.

Sin embargo, esa descripción del premio no debe tratarse como una demostración pública de robo de datos de clientes. La captura de pantalla oculta la causa raíz del informe y las declaraciones disponibles no establecen que se haya accedido a información real del cliente.

El desafío Sandbox de Vercel por un millón de dólares se inauguró el 18 de agosto de 2026, con una fecha de cierre programada para el 1 de septiembre. Sus reglas publicadas requieren una prueba de concepto en vivo que muestre un límite de seguridad roto, en lugar de un informe basado únicamente en la revisión del código.

KVM, abreviatura de Máquina virtual basada en kernel, proporciona virtualización de Linux. Una máquina virtual invitada debe permanecer separada del host que la ejecuta. Una escapada exitosa de huésped a anfitrión rompe esa separación; El acceso raíz le da al atacante el más alto nivel de control sobre el host.

La arquitectura publicada de Vercel coloca cada sandbox dentro de su propia microVM Firecracker en un host Amazon EC2 sin sistema operativo. Cada microVM tiene un kernel invitado dedicado, mientras que un contenedor de Linux en su interior ejecuta el código del usuario. Vercel identifica explícitamente la microVM, no el contenedor, como el principal límite de seguridad.

Esta distinción es importante para los agentes de IA que ejecutan código generado o descargado. Pasar de un contenedor a su sistema operativo invitado no es lo mismo que llegar al host subyacente. La afirmación de Yibelo describe el cruce de fronteras más grave, aunque los pasos técnicos exactos siguen sin revelarse.

El anuncio no identifica un CVE, las versiones del kernel afectadas, los requisitos del procesador ni un parche. Tampoco establece si se requiere acceso de administrador invitado. La referencia de Rauch a KVM no prueba que cada implementación de KVM, instalación de Firecracker o proveedor de nube sea vulnerable. Los detalles que faltan también impiden una evaluación independiente de la confiabilidad del exploit en diferentes configuraciones de host.

Como antecedente, Cybersecuritynews cubrió anteriormente la vulnerabilidad separada de Januscape KVM, que involucraba corrupción de la memoria del host a través de la virtualización anidada. No hay evidencia divulgada que vincule ese problema con el hallazgo de Yibelo, por lo que sus condiciones de explotación y correcciones no deben aplicarse a este informe.

Hasta que llegue la divulgación técnica, los operadores deben seguir a Vercel y sus proveedores de Linux para obtener orientación, en lugar de asumir que un parche no relacionado soluciona este defecto. La conclusión inmediata es un informe de vulnerabilidad confirmado y un supuesto escape de la raíz del host, no una explotación generalizada confirmada.

El artículo prometido debería aclarar la causa raíz, los sistemas afectados y las protecciones disponibles, permitiendo a los defensores evaluar la exposición sin tener que adivinar. Esos detalles determinarán qué despliegues realmente necesitan medidas urgentes.
